questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Macrophages express MHC class II and present processed antigen to CD4+ helper T cells.

options.label: B
options.explanation: T cells recognise antigen presented on MHC; they are not professional antigen-presenting cells.

options.label: C
options.explanation: B cells capture antigen via surface immunoglobulin and present it on MHC class II to helper T cells.

options.label: D
options.explanation: NK cells are innate cytotoxic lymphocytes that kill MHC-I-deficient cells; they do not present antigen.

questions.pearl: Professional APCs: dendritic cells (most potent), macrophages and B cells, all expressing MHC class II.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Clinical features of upper motor neuron lesion:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fasciculation reflects anterior horn cell or lower motor neuron disease, not UMN lesions.

options.label: B
options.explanation: UMN lesions cause only mild disuse atrophy; marked wasting is a LMN sign.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Corticospinal fibres decussate in the medulla, so a cerebral UMN lesion weakens the opposite side.

options.label: D
options.explanation: UMN lesions give spastic paralysis with hyperreflexia; flaccidity occurs only transiently in the shock phase.

questions.pearl: UMN: spasticity, hyperreflexia, extensor plantar, pyramidal weakness. LMN: wasting, fasciculation, hypotonia, areflexia.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sunken eyes are one of the signs used to classify some dehydration in IMCI.

options.label: B
options.text: Skin pinch goes back very slowly
options.explanation: Very slow skin pinch (>2 seconds) indicates severe dehydration; in some dehydration it goes back slowly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Restless, irritable and drinking eagerly are classic signs of some dehydration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lethargy or unconsciousness indicates severe dehydration.

questions.pearl: IMCI some dehydration = two of: restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch goes back slowly; treat with Plan B.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Characteristics of CSF in tuberculous meningitis:

options.label: A
options.explanation: High fibrinogen content makes TB CSF form a cobweb clot when left standing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Opening pressure is usually raised, partly from basal exudate and hydrocephalus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protein is markedly raised (often 1-5 g/L), especially with spinal block.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glucose is low (CSF:blood ratio usually <0.5) in TB meningitis.

questions.pearl: TB meningitis CSF: lymphocytes, very high protein, low glucose, cobweb clot, clear or slightly turbid fluid.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Typical patient is a postmenopausal woman with osteoporosis falling on an outstretched hand.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dorsal displacement of the distal fragment produces the classic dinner-fork deformity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The distal radial fragment is dorsally angulated and displaced, with radial shift.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Complex regional pain syndrome (Sudeck osteodystrophy) is a recognised complication.

questions.pearl: Colles complications: malunion, stiffness, Sudeck atrophy, EPL tendon rupture, median nerve compression.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.text: Holding the baby at a 30 degree angle
options.explanation: No fixed angle is required; the baby's body should be close, facing the breast, head and body in line.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Good attachment (latch) is one of the two key components assessed in breastfeeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Correct positioning of mother and baby is the other key component of effective breastfeeding.

options.label: D
options.text: Baby's mouth covers most of the areola
options.explanation: In good attachment more areola is visible above than below and the mouth is wide open over the areola.

questions.pearl: Signs of good attachment: chin touching breast, mouth wide open, lower lip everted, more areola above than below.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Location of headquarters of health organisations:

options.label: A
options.explanation: WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland, established in 1948.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Texas Medical Center is in Houston, Texas, USA.

options.label: C
options.explanation: UNICEF headquarters is in New York, USA.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh is headquartered in Dhaka.

questions.pearl: WHO SEARO regional office is in New Delhi; World Health Day is 7 April.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cervical dilatation is plotted against time with alert and action lines.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fetal heart rate is recorded every 30 minutes in the fetal section.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Frequency and duration of contractions per 10 minutes are charted.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Crossing the alert and action lines flags prolonged or obstructed labour for timely intervention.

questions.pearl: WHO partograph: active phase from 4 cm; the action line lies 4 hours to the right of the alert line.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cirrhotic ascites is a transudate (SAAG ≥11 g/L, low protein).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cardiac ascites is a high-SAAG transudate from raised hydrostatic pressure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Peritoneal carcinomatosis produces a protein-rich exudate.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TB peritonitis gives an exudate with lymphocytes, high protein and raised ADA.

questions.pearl: SAAG ≥11 g/L = portal hypertension; SAAG <11 g/L = peritoneal disease (TB, cancer, pancreatitis).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Parallel rays focus in front of the retina; corrected with concave lenses.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Age-related loss of accommodation, grouped with errors of refraction and corrected with convex reading lenses.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Parallel rays focus behind the retina; corrected with convex lenses.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Unequal refractive power in different meridians; corrected with cylindrical lenses.

questions.pearl: Myopia: concave lens; hypermetropia and presbyopia: convex lens; astigmatism: cylindrical lens.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Loss of sympathetic supply to Müller muscle causes partial ptosis with miosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Paralysis of levator palpebrae superioris causes complete ptosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The intermediate syndrome after OP poisoning causes cranial nerve weakness including ptosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glaucoma raises intraocular pressure and damages the optic nerve; it does not cause ptosis.

questions.pearl: Ptosis with miosis = Horner; ptosis with dilated pupil and down-and-out eye = third nerve palsy.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Intraductal carcinoma can present with blood-stained discharge, especially in older women.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mastitis gives purulent discharge with a tender inflamed breast, not bloody discharge.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Discharge is usually cheesy or green, but can be blood-stained.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cyclical hormonal changes cause breast tenderness, not bloody nipple discharge.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of bloody nipple discharge is intraductal papilloma; always exclude carcinoma.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cholesteatoma can erode the fallopian canal and cause lower motor neuron facial palsy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Unsafe (atticoantral) CSOM is associated with cholesteatoma, which erodes bone.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Labyrinthitis or toxin spread through the round window can cause SNHL.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lateral (sigmoid) sinus thrombosis is a recognised intracranial complication.

questions.pearl: Commonest intracranial complication of CSOM is meningitis; commonest extracranial is mastoid abscess.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Isoniazid is a recognised cause of gynaecomastia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Digoxin has an oestrogen-like steroid structure and causes gynaecomastia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Spironolactone blocks androgen receptors and is the classic drug cause.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Propranolol is not associated with gynaecomastia.

questions.pearl: Drug gynaecomastia mnemonic DISCO: Digoxin, Isoniazid, Spironolactone, Cimetidine, Oestrogens.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Organisms causing meningitis in school-age children:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pneumococcus is a leading cause of bacterial meningitis beyond the neonatal period.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hib mainly affects children under 5 years and is now rare after vaccination.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Meningococcus is a major cause in children and adolescents, often with petechial rash.

options.label: D
options.explanation: E. coli is a neonatal pathogen along with group B streptococcus and Listeria.

questions.pearl: Neonate: GBS, E. coli, Listeria. Older children: pneumococcus and meningococcus.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Excess TSH drives the thyroid to produce more T3.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Free T4 is raised along with T3.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Inappropriately normal or high TSH from a pituitary adenoma is the defining feature.

options.label: D
options.text: Pathology lies in the thyroid gland
options.explanation: The lesion is in the pituitary (TSH-secreting adenoma); the thyroid is normal.

questions.pearl: High T4 with high TSH = TSHoma or thyroid hormone resistance; primary hyperthyroidism has suppressed TSH.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Spores are survival forms, not required for growth or replication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Plasmids are extrachromosomal DNA carrying optional genes such as antibiotic resistance.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Teichoic acid is an integral cell wall component of Gram-positive bacteria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Flagella provide motility but are not needed for survival.

questions.pearl: Essential: cell wall, cell membrane, ribosomes, nucleoid. Non-essential: capsule, flagella, pili, plasmids, spores.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Platelets fall progressively in severe dengue; a rising count indicates recovery.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haematocrit rises (≥20%) due to haemoconcentration from plasma leakage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mucosal bleeding is a warning sign, but does not define shock.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Plasma leakage with narrow pulse pressure or hypotension is the basis of dengue shock syndrome.

questions.pearl: Dengue shock: pulse pressure ≤20 mmHg, cold extremities, rising haematocrit with falling platelets.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Anaemia causes a hyperdynamic circulation with low diastolic pressure, not sustained hypertension.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Beta-blockers lower blood pressure; abrupt withdrawal may cause rebound.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mineralocorticoid deficiency causes hypotension and postural drop.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Salt and water retention in acute glomerulonephritis causes hypertension.

questions.pearl: Nephritic syndrome: haematuria, hypertension, oliguria, oedema and mild proteinuria.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute infection, especially pneumonia, is a common trigger of AF.

options.label: B
options.explanation: AF is irregularly irregular with no P waves.

options.label: C
options.text: Digoxin is used for rate control
options.explanation: Digoxin slows AV conduction, useful in sedentary patients or with heart failure.

options.label: D
options.text: Need for anticoagulation is assessed by CHA2DS2-VASc score
options.explanation: Stroke risk in non-valvular AF is stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc.

questions.pearl: Rate control first line: beta-blocker or rate-limiting calcium channel blocker; digoxin if sedentary or heart failure.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Candida causes cutaneous candidiasis in moist skin folds.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Staph aureus is a bacterium, not a fungus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: T. pallidum is a spirochaete bacterium that penetrates mucosa or abraded skin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Trichophyton is a dermatophyte infecting keratinised skin, hair and nails.

questions.pearl: Dermatophytes: Trichophyton (skin, hair, nail), Microsporum (skin, hair), Epidermophyton (skin, nail).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Apoptosis is programmed cell death, an end-point of irreversible injury.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Necrosis follows irreversible injury with membrane damage and inflammation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Metaplasia is a reversible adaptive change of one cell type to another.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hyperplasia is a reversible adaptive increase in cell number.

questions.pearl: Hallmarks of irreversible injury: severe mitochondrial damage and membrane disruption; nuclear pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Broad-spectrum antiepileptic, first choice for generalised epilepsy (avoid in women of childbearing age).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Drug of choice for prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Benzodiazepines are first-line for terminating status epilepticus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Levothyroxine is thyroid hormone replacement; it has no anticonvulsant action.

questions.pearl: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepine first, then phenytoin, levetiracetam or valproate.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dihydropyridine CCBs lower BP but do not specifically reduce proteinuria.

options.label: B
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors dilate the efferent arteriole, lowering intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ARBs share the antiproteinuric efferent arteriolar effect of ACE inhibitors.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Alpha-blockers have no specific antiproteinuric effect.

questions.pearl: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are renoprotective in diabetic nephropathy; SGLT2 inhibitors add further benefit.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stabilises the cardiac membrane within minutes; 10 mL of 10% given IV over 5-10 minutes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Insulin shifts potassium into cells via Na-K ATPase, lowering it within 30 minutes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Calcium resonium removes potassium from the body through the gut.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gastric aspiration does not remove significant potassium and is not a treatment.

questions.pearl: Hyperkalaemia: protect (calcium), shift (insulin-glucose, salbutamol), remove (resins, dialysis).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Permethrin 5% cream is the treatment of choice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Oral ivermectin is used for crusted scabies or mass treatment.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Antibiotics treat secondary bacterial infection only; they do not kill the mite.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Silicone gel is used for hypertrophic scars and keloids.

questions.pearl: Treat all close contacts simultaneously; itch may persist 2-4 weeks after successful treatment.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The mitral valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The aortic valve is a semilunar valve between left ventricle and aorta.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The pulmonary valve is a semilunar valve between right ventricle and pulmonary trunk.

questions.pearl: Closure of AV valves produces S1; closure of semilunar valves produces S2.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: ABO incompatibility causes pathological haemolytic jaundice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It is an unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia; raised direct bilirubin is always pathological.

options.label: C
options.text: Appears on the first day of life
options.explanation: Jaundice within 24 hours is pathological; physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours.

options.label: D
options.text: Due to shorter lifespan of fetal red cells
options.explanation: Fetal RBCs live about 80-90 days, and the immature liver has low glucuronyl transferase.

questions.pearl: Physiological jaundice: appears day 2-3, peaks day 3-5, resolves by 2 weeks in term babies.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pupils are assessed separately; they are not part of the GCS.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sensation is not scored in the GCS.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Best motor response is scored 1-6.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Best verbal response is scored 1-5.

questions.pearl: GCS = eye (4) + verbal (5) + motor (6); range 3-15; GCS ≤8 suggests need for airway protection.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute congestive glaucoma causes glaukomflecken, a form of complicated cataract.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Retinitis pigmentosa and longstanding retinal detachment cause complicated cataract.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diabetes causes snowflake and early senile-type metabolic cataract.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypertension causes retinopathy, not cataract.

questions.pearl: Complicated cataract shows a polychromatic lustre and breadcrumb appearance at the posterior pole.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oxytocin infusion is used to induce labour once the cervix is favourable.

options.label: B
options.text: Routine management of the second stage
options.explanation: Its routine use is in the third stage; in the second stage it is used only for inertia, not routinely.

options.label: C
options.text: Active management of the third stage of labour
options.explanation: 10 IU IM after delivery of the baby reduces postpartum haemorrhage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Oxytocin infusion contracts the atonic uterus and is first-line therapy.

questions.pearl: Oxytocin has antidiuretic action: prolonged high-dose infusion in dextrose can cause water intoxication.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Muscarinic overstimulation of the sphincter pupillae causes miosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nicotinic stimulation at the neuromuscular junction causes fasciculation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Excess salivation and secretions occur; dry mouth suggests anticholinergic poisoning.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Muscarinic effects cause diarrhoea and abdominal cramps.

questions.pearl: Muscarinic features mnemonic DUMBELS: diarrhoea, urination, miosis, bronchorrhoea, emesis, lacrimation, salivation.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Xerosis is caused by vitamin A deficiency, not third nerve palsy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Levator palpebrae superioris is supplied by the oculomotor nerve.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The ciliospinal reflex is sympathetically mediated, so it is preserved in third nerve palsy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The eye is deviated down and out and convergence is lost due to medial rectus palsy.

questions.pearl: Painful third nerve palsy with dilated pupil: exclude posterior communicating artery aneurysm.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paralysis of levator palpebrae superioris causes complete ptosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loss of sympathetic supply to Müller muscle causes mild ptosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil is a pupillary abnormality of neurosyphilis without ptosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sixth nerve palsy causes lateral rectus weakness and diplopia, not ptosis.

questions.pearl: Argyll Robertson pupil: small irregular pupils that accommodate but do not react to light.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Vessels used as grafts in CABG:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The left internal mammary artery to LAD has the best long-term patency.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The radial artery is a common second arterial conduit.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The carotid artery supplies the brain and is never harvested as a conduit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The great saphenous vein is the standard venous conduit; the small saphenous is rarely used.

questions.pearl: LIMA graft patency exceeds 90% at 10 years versus about 50-60% for saphenous vein grafts.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cystic hygroma lies in the posterior triangle at the root of the neck.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Branchial cyst lies laterally at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Thyroglossal cyst is midline and moves upwards on tongue protrusion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Swelling of the isthmus is midline and moves with swallowing.

questions.pearl: Midline neck: thyroglossal cyst, dermoid cyst, isthmus swelling, submental lymph node, plunging ranula.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepatitis A, B and E (especially in pregnancy) are leading causes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Paracetamol overdose is the commonest cause in the UK.

options.label: C
options.explanation: By definition fulminant failure occurs without pre-existing liver disease; cirrhosis gives acute-on-chronic failure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe dengue can cause acute liver failure.

questions.pearl: Acute liver failure: encephalopathy and INR ≥1.5 within 26 weeks of illness onset in a previously normal liver.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rapid infusion of cold stored blood lowers core temperature.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Citrate chelates calcium, causing hypocalcaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Potassium leaks from stored red cells into the plasma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Dilution of platelets and clotting factors causes dilutional coagulopathy.

questions.pearl: Lethal triad of trauma: hypothermia, acidosis and coagulopathy.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cobblestoning from deep ulcers and fissures is typical of Crohn disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Regenerating mucosa between ulcers forms inflammatory pseudopolyps.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of haustrations in chronic UC gives a lead-pipe colon on barium enema.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Smoking is protective in UC (it worsens Crohn disease).

questions.pearl: UC: continuous, starts in rectum, mucosal only; Crohn: skip lesions, transmural, granulomas.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.text: Peripheral blood film is a histopathological test
options.explanation: A blood film is a haematology (cytological) test, not tissue histology.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Histopathology of a biopsy is the gold standard for diagnosing malignancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells on biopsy are diagnostic.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rectal suction biopsy showing absent ganglion cells confirms the diagnosis.

questions.pearl: Histopathology examines tissue architecture; cytology (FNAC, smears) examines individual cells.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Normal saline has an osmolality of about 308 mOsm/L, roughly isotonic with plasma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: 3% saline is hypertonic, used for symptomatic hyponatraemia and raised ICP.

options.label: C
options.explanation: 5% DNS is hypertonic in the bag (about 560 mOsm/L).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mannitol 20% is a hypertonic osmotic diuretic.

questions.pearl: Isotonic crystalloids: 0.9% NaCl, Hartmann's/Ringer's lactate; 5% dextrose is isotonic in the bag but physiologically hypotonic.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: The bladder base sags below the urethral level, leaving residual urine.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Residual urine predisposes to recurrent UTI.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Associated urethrocele and loss of bladder neck support can cause stress incontinence.

options.label: D
options.text: Due to weakness of the posterior vaginal wall
options.explanation: Cystocele is an anterior vaginal wall prolapse; posterior wall weakness causes rectocele.

questions.pearl: Anterior wall: cystocele, urethrocele. Posterior wall: rectocele, enterocele.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Blood pressure is a basic haemodynamic parameter monitored in all shocked patients.

options.label: B
options.explanation: EEG is not part of shock monitoring.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Core temperature is monitored to detect hypothermia and sepsis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hourly urine output (target >0.5 mL/kg/h) reflects end-organ perfusion.

questions.pearl: Minimum monitoring in shock: ECG, pulse oximetry, BP, temperature and urine output.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Uncomplicated COPD does not cause clubbing; its presence suggests bronchial carcinoma or bronchiectasis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute pneumonia does not cause clubbing; lung abscess and empyema do.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cirrhosis, especially biliary cirrhosis, is a recognised GI cause.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bronchial carcinoma (non-small cell) is the commonest cause of clubbing.

questions.pearl: Clubbing in COPD should prompt a search for lung cancer.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Features and complications of strangulated hernia:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Strangulation produces a tense, tender, irreducible swelling with severe pain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Arterial obstruction leads to ischaemic necrosis of the strangulated loop.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Strangulated bowel causes obstruction with colicky pain, vomiting and distension.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Strangulation is a surgical emergency and does not resolve spontaneously.

questions.pearl: Femoral hernia has the highest risk of strangulation; Richter hernia strangulates without obstruction.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Management of the third stage of labour:

options.label: A
options.explanation: 10 IU IM oxytocin within one minute of delivery is the uterotonic of choice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Controlled cord traction with counter-traction is a component of active management.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Episiotomy is performed in the second stage to enlarge the outlet.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fundal massage keeps the uterus contracted and reduces PPH.

questions.pearl: Active management of third stage: uterotonic, controlled cord traction, uterine massage; reduces PPH by about 60%.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: WHO defines health as complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely absence of disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Health has physical, mental, social, spiritual, emotional and other dimensions.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Health is both a means and an end of socioeconomic development.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Quality of life and physical quality of life index are used as health indicators.

questions.pearl: Physical Quality of Life Index combines infant mortality, life expectancy at age 1 and literacy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: RBC migration plays no role in haemostasis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Platelets adhere to exposed collagen via von Willebrand factor to form the primary plug.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vasodilatation would increase bleeding; the injured vessel constricts.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Immediate vascular spasm reduces blood flow from the damaged vessel.

questions.pearl: Haemostasis: vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation cascade (fibrin), then fibrinolysis.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The greater palatine artery reaches the septum through the incisive canal.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The septal branch of the sphenopalatine artery contributes to the plexus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The anterior ethmoidal artery is a contributor from the internal carotid system.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The superficial temporal artery supplies the scalp, not the nasal septum.

questions.pearl: Little's area: anterior ethmoidal, sphenopalatine, greater palatine and superior labial arteries; commonest site of epistaxis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Components of a routine lipid profile:

options.label: A
options.explanation: VLDL cholesterol is reported, usually calculated as triglyceride/5 (mg/dL).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chylomicrons are not measured routinely; fasting sample is chylomicron-free.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HDL cholesterol is measured directly in every lipid profile.

options.label: D
options.explanation: LDL is usually calculated by the Friedewald equation.

questions.pearl: Friedewald: LDL = TC − HDL − TG/5 (mg/dL); invalid when TG >400 mg/dL.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Inferior MI often presents with epigastric pain mimicking dyspepsia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gastritis causes burning epigastric pain.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pancreatitis causes severe epigastric pain radiating to the back.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Liver capsule stretch causes right upper quadrant and epigastric discomfort.

questions.pearl: Always do an ECG in older patients with epigastric pain to exclude inferior MI.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Untidy wounds have tissue loss and devitalised tissue.

options.label: B
options.explanation: They need debridement and delayed primary closure or healing by secondary intention.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Untidy wounds have ragged, irregular edges.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Crushing, tearing and avulsion produce untidy wounds.

questions.pearl: Tidy wound: clean incised, minimal tissue loss, primary repair. Untidy: crushed, contaminated, debride first.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Avascular necrosis of the lunate is Kienböck disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Intracapsular femoral neck fracture disrupts retinacular vessels, causing femoral head AVN.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Retrograde blood supply makes the proximal pole of the scaphoid vulnerable.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ribs have a rich blood supply and are not a classic AVN site.

questions.pearl: AVN sites: femoral head, scaphoid proximal pole, talus body, lunate.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Soft tissue stripping and infection impair healing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Greenstick fractures occur in children and heal rapidly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Avascular fragments, as in scaphoid or femoral neck, are prone to non-union.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Interposed muscle or periosteum prevents fragment contact.

questions.pearl: Non-union causes: poor blood supply, infection, excessive movement, interposition, distraction, pathological bone.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Proteinuria >3.5 g/day causes hypoalbuminaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Anaemia is not a defining feature of nephrotic syndrome.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haematuria is typical of nephritic, not nephrotic, syndrome.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Facial puffiness is due to oedema; moon face is a Cushingoid steroid effect.

questions.pearl: Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, oedema, hyperlipidaemia and hypercoagulability.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: A clenched fist over the sternum describes ischaemic chest pain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Unstable angina occurs at rest or with minimal exertion; relief by rest is stable angina.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Retrosternal, crushing or tight pain is typical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A troponin rise indicates myocardial necrosis, i.e. NSTEMI.

questions.pearl: Unstable angina: new-onset, crescendo or rest angina with normal troponin.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: Cannot complete a sentence in one breath
options.explanation: This is a feature of acute severe asthma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: PEF 33-50% is acute severe; life-threatening is PEF <33%.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Silent chest indicates very poor air entry and impending respiratory failure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: RR ≥25/min is acute severe; exhaustion and bradycardia are life-threatening.

questions.pearl: Life-threatening asthma: PEF <33%, SpO2 <92%, silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, arrhythmia, hypotension, normal PaCO2.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Congestive splenomegaly with hypersplenism is common.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Raised sinusoidal pressure contributes to ascites formation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Portal hypertension does not cause mechanical bowel obstruction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Portal hypertension is a consequence of liver disease; it does not itself cause liver failure.

questions.pearl: Portal hypertension: HVPG >5 mmHg; varices form above 10 and bleed above 12 mmHg.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypoalbuminaemia from cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome causes white nails.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemophilia causes haemarthrosis and muscle bleeds, not nail changes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ITP causes petechiae and purpura, not leukonychia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Myeloma is not a recognised cause of leukonychia.

questions.pearl: Muehrcke lines (paired white bands) indicate hypoalbuminaemia; Terry nails are seen in cirrhosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Xerosis of the conjunctiva and skin is due to vitamin A deficiency.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dry beriberi causes symmetrical sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Thickened, pigmented skin is a feature of pellagra (niacin deficiency).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Wet beriberi causes high-output heart failure with oedema.

questions.pearl: Thiamine deficiency: dry beriberi, wet beriberi, Wernicke encephalopathy (confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Extensor plantar is a pyramidal (UMN) sign.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nystagmus is a cerebellar or vestibular sign.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Intention tremor is cerebellar; extrapyramidal tremor is a resting tremor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Akinesia and bradykinesia are cardinal features of parkinsonism.

questions.pearl: Parkinsonism: resting tremor, rigidity (cogwheel), bradykinesia, postural instability.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Iron deficiency anaemia suggests GI blood loss or malignancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dysphagia suggests oesophageal cancer or stricture and needs urgent endoscopy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: New-onset dyspepsia above 55 years warrants endoscopy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diarrhoea is not an alarm feature of dyspepsia.

questions.pearl: Alarm features: weight loss, anaemia, dysphagia, persistent vomiting, GI bleeding, mass, age >55 with new symptoms.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The principal human pathogen of the complex.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Causes bovine TB, transmitted by unpasteurised milk; BCG is derived from it.

options.label: C
options.explanation: M. kansasii is a non-tuberculous (atypical) photochromogen.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A member of the complex causing human TB in West Africa.

questions.pearl: MTB complex: M. tuberculosis, bovis, africanum, microti, canetti; all others are NTM.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Commonest cause of microcytic hypochromic anaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic macrocytic anaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Folate deficiency causes megaloblastic macrocytic anaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, causing macrocytosis.

questions.pearl: Microcytic causes mnemonic TAILS: thalassaemia, anaemia of chronic disease, iron deficiency, lead, sideroblastic.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: RTA causes normal anion gap (hyperchloraemic) metabolic acidosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loss of gastric HCl causes metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of bicarbonate in stool causes normal anion gap acidosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Haemolysis releases potassium but is not a recognised cause of metabolic acidosis.

questions.pearl: High anion gap acidosis mnemonic MUDPILES; normal anion gap: diarrhoea, RTA, ureteric diversion, acetazolamide.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dextran is a synthetic colloid.

options.label: B
options.explanation: DNS is a crystalloid solution of dextrose and sodium chloride.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Normal saline is the commonest crystalloid.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Albumin is a natural colloid.

questions.pearl: Colloids: albumin, dextran, gelatin, hydroxyethyl starch; crystalloids: saline, Hartmann's, dextrose solutions.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of painful bleeding per rectum:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Internal haemorrhoids bleed painlessly as they arise above the dentate line.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fissure causes severe pain on defecation with fresh blood streaking the stool.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Colicky abdominal pain with redcurrant jelly stool is classic in infants.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bloody diarrhoea with cramping pain and tenesmus is typical of colitis.

questions.pearl: Painless fresh bleeding: haemorrhoids, polyps, diverticular disease, angiodysplasia.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Colposcopy magnifies the cervix to assess the transformation zone.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vaginal walls can be examined for VAIN.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ovaries are intra-abdominal and need laparoscopy or ultrasound.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tubes are assessed by laparoscopy or HSG.

questions.pearl: Colposcopy uses 3-5% acetic acid (acetowhite areas) and Lugol's iodine (Schiller test).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mydriasis can precipitate angle-closure glaucoma in eyes with narrow angles.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Raised IOP is the main risk factor and feature of glaucoma.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uncomplicated cataract does not raise IOP; only intumescent or hypermature lenses cause secondary glaucoma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Third nerve palsy causes ptosis and mydriasis but does not raise IOP.

questions.pearl: Normal IOP is 10-21 mmHg; avoid mydriatics in shallow anterior chambers.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: PTH raises serum calcium via bone resorption, renal reabsorption and calcitriol synthesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Androgens affect bone mass but are not regulators of serum calcium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Insulin regulates glucose and potassium, not calcium.

options.label: D
options.explanation: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D increases intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption.

questions.pearl: Calcium regulators: PTH, calcitriol (both raise calcium) and calcitonin (lowers calcium).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sarcomas are malignant tumours of mesenchymal origin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Seminoma is a malignant germ cell tumour despite its -oma suffix.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Teratoma can be benign, e.g. mature cystic teratoma (dermoid) of the ovary.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Synovioma (synovial sarcoma) is malignant.

questions.pearl: Malignant despite -oma: lymphoma, melanoma, seminoma, mesothelioma, hepatoma.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Factors II, VII, IX and X fall; factor VII has the shortest half-life, so PT prolongs first.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemophilia (factor VIII or IX deficiency) prolongs APTT with normal PT.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Consumption of clotting factors prolongs both PT and APTT.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Impaired hepatic synthesis of clotting factors prolongs PT.

questions.pearl: PT tests extrinsic pathway (factor VII); APTT tests intrinsic pathway (VIII, IX, XI, XII).

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Causes of rupture of the uterus:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Interstitial pregnancy ruptures through the myometrium, effectively a uterine rupture.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Invasive mole can penetrate the myometrium and perforate the uterus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: IUCD can perforate the uterus at insertion but is not a cause of uterine rupture in pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pregnancy in a rudimentary horn commonly ruptures in the second trimester.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of uterine rupture: previous caesarean scar; in developing countries, obstructed labour.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The vitreous is avascular gel nourished by diffusion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The retina has a dual supply: central retinal artery and choroid.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The conjunctiva is vascular, as seen in conjunctival injection.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The cornea is avascular, which aids transparency and graft success.

questions.pearl: Avascular ocular structures: cornea, lens, vitreous; cornea gets oxygen mainly from tear film and air.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Puerperal pyrexia includes fever from any cause within 10 days of delivery.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Poor asepsis leads to genital tract sepsis, the commonest cause.

options.label: C
options.explanation: UTI is a common cause, especially after catheterisation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Wound infection of the perineum causes local pain and fever.

questions.pearl: Puerperal pyrexia: temperature ≥38°C on any two of the first 10 days postpartum, excluding the first 24 hours.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The retina is the light-sensitive layer where images form; it does not refract.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The conjunctiva is a mucous membrane with no refractive role.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The cornea provides about two-thirds (around 43 D) of total refractive power.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The lens provides about 15-20 D and allows accommodation.

questions.pearl: Refractive media: tear film, cornea, aqueous, lens, vitreous; total power about 60 D.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Complications in the first stage of labour:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Slow progress of cervical dilatation crossing the action line indicates prolonged first stage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cervical dystocia from inertia or disproportion is a first-stage problem.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Air embolism is a rare event linked to placental separation or procedures, not a first-stage complication.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PPH occurs after delivery of the baby, in the third stage or puerperium.

questions.pearl: First stage: onset of true labour to full cervical dilatation; active phase from 4 cm (WHO 2018: 5 cm).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Old MI shows Q waves; persistent ST elevation suggests ventricular aneurysm.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Severe hyperkalaemia can cause ST elevation (pseudo-infarction) along with peaked T waves.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diffuse saddle-shaped ST elevation with PR depression is typical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Heart failure itself does not cause ST elevation.

questions.pearl: ST elevation causes: STEMI, pericarditis, LV aneurysm, Prinzmetal angina, Brugada, LBBB, early repolarisation.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Clinical features of right heart failure:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepatic venous congestion stretches the liver capsule.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Raised systemic venous pressure elevates the JVP.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Crepitations reflect pulmonary congestion of left heart failure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: An S3 gallop is classically a sign of left ventricular failure.

questions.pearl: Right heart failure: raised JVP, tender hepatomegaly, ascites, dependent pitting oedema.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: EPO is a glycoprotein hormone, not an enzyme.

options.label: B
options.explanation: About 90% is produced by renal peritubular interstitial cells; the liver is the main source only in the fetus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Platelet production is driven by thrombopoietin.

options.label: D
options.text: Stimulates bone marrow for RBC production
options.explanation: EPO stimulates erythroid progenitors in response to hypoxia.

questions.pearl: Anaemia of CKD is due to EPO deficiency; EPO is raised in secondary polycythaemia.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: An extra X chromosome from meiotic non-disjunction.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Long legs and eunuchoid proportions give tall stature.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Gynaecomastia is characteristic.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Small firm testes with azoospermia and hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism.

questions.pearl: Klinefelter: commonest cause of male hypogonadism; high FSH and LH, low testosterone, increased breast cancer risk.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Causes and risk factors of placenta praevia:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The larger placental area is more likely to encroach on the lower segment.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A lower segment scar increases implantation in the lower segment.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Placenta praevia is not a genetic condition.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Both are recognised risk factors.

questions.pearl: Placenta praevia: painless, recurrent, causeless bright red APH; never do a PV examination before excluding it.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Hormones secreted from the posterior pituitary:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Prolactin is secreted by lactotrophs of the anterior pituitary.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Synthesised in supraoptic nuclei and released from the posterior pituitary.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Synthesised in paraventricular nuclei and released from the posterior pituitary.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TSH is an anterior pituitary hormone.

questions.pearl: Posterior pituitary stores hormones made in the hypothalamus; it synthesises none itself.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Lipid deposits from leaky vessels, typical of background diabetic retinopathy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Flame haemorrhages lie in the nerve fibre layer and are typical of hypertensive retinopathy; DR has dot-blot haemorrhages.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Macular star is seen in malignant hypertension and neuroretinitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Nerve fibre layer infarcts seen in pre-proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

questions.pearl: Earliest sign of diabetic retinopathy is microaneurysms; neovascularisation defines proliferative DR.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: A thinned, overstretched lower segment ruptures if obstruction is not relieved.

options.label: B
options.explanation: APH occurs before labour; obstruction causes PPH rather than APH.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Prolonged hypoxia and sepsis cause intrapartum fetal death.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pressure necrosis of the bladder base leads to VVF.

questions.pearl: Bandl's ring (pathological retraction ring) is a sign of impending uterine rupture in obstructed labour.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tachycardia is an autonomic feature of anxiety, not depression.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Suicidal ideation is a key feature and must always be assessed.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hopelessness about the future is a core cognitive feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fear and apprehension are features of anxiety disorders.

questions.pearl: Core depressive symptoms (≥2 weeks): low mood, anhedonia, fatigue; screen with PHQ-9.
